description: Morocco's COVID-19 vaccination campaign, launched in January 2021, achieved one of the highest vaccination rates in Africa, with over 60 percent of the adult population receiving at least one dose by mid-2021. The campaign benefited from early procurement of vaccines, strong logistical capacity, and effective public communications. Morocco's vaccination success was widely cited as a model for other African countries. The king personally received his vaccination publicly to encourage uptake.

title: Spain Backs Moroccan Autonomy Plan for Western Sahara
description: Spain formally endorsed Morocco's autonomy plan for Western Sahara in March 2022, marking a significant diplomatic breakthrough for Morocco. Spain's position had previously been one of strict neutrality, and its shift came after intense diplomatic pressure from Rabat following the 2021 Ceuta migration crisis. The Spanish endorsement was hailed by Morocco as a major victory. Algeria recalled its ambassador from Spain in protest and the Moroccan-Spanish bilateral relationship was substantially repaired after the tensions of 2021.

title: FIFA 2030 World Cup Bid — Spain-Morocco-Portugal Co-Host
description: Spain, Morocco, and Portugal announced a joint bid to host the 2030 FIFA World Cup, with Morocco hosting a significant portion of matches. The bid was eventually awarded, representing a major milestone for Moroccan football and a symbol of the country's growing international stature. Morocco's co-hosting role required massive investment in football infrastructure including new and upgraded stadiums across multiple cities. The announcement generated enormous national pride and expectations of an economic boost from hosting the world's largest sporting event.

title: Noor Solar Complex Reaches Major Capacity Milestone
description: The Noor Ouarzazate solar complex reached its final designed capacity of 580 megawatts in 2022, making it one of the world's largest concentrated solar power installations. Morocco also continued to develop wind energy capacity, with the Tarfaya wind farm among the largest in Africa. Renewable energy accounted for a growing share of Moroccan electricity generation, reducing dependence on imported fossil fuels. Morocco moved toward its target of 52 percent renewable electricity by 2030, positioning itself as a potential exporter of green hydrogen and electricity to Europe.

title: Al Haouz Earthquake Kills 3,000 People
description: A devastating earthquake measuring 6.8 on the Richter scale struck the Al Haouz province south of Marrakech on 8 September 2023, killing nearly 3,000 people and injuring thousands more. The earthquake was the deadliest in Morocco in over six decades, with remote Atlas mountain villages particularly badly hit. Entire villages were flattened, leaving survivors without shelter as rescue efforts were complicated by difficult terrain and damaged roads. International rescue teams from several countries, including France, Spain, the UK, and Qatar, were deployed to assist.

title: Morocco World Cup Qatar — Historic Semi-Final Run
description: At the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar, held in November-December 2022, Morocco became the first African and Arab nation to reach the semi-finals, defeating Spain, Portugal, and Belgium along the way before losing to France. The achievement generated extraordinary celebrations across Morocco and the Arab world. The team's success — built largely on the diaspora generation with dual European citizenship — prompted a national conversation about identity, belonging, and the contributions of Moroccans living abroad. The run to the semi-finals raised immense expectations for the 2030 World Cup.

title: Earthquake Reconstruction Programme Launched
description: Following the September 2023 Al Haouz earthquake, Mohammed VI announced a comprehensive reconstruction programme backed by 120 billion dirhams over five years. The programme included rebuilding destroyed villages, constructing new housing, restoring schools and health facilities, and improving road access to previously isolated communities. International donors pledged additional support. The reconstruction effort was seen as both a humanitarian imperative and an opportunity to modernise infrastructure in the historically neglected High Atlas region.

title: Morocco Advances 2030 World Cup Infrastructure
description: Morocco accelerated preparations for its co-hosting role in the 2030 FIFA World Cup, with construction beginning on new and upgraded stadiums in Casablanca, Rabat, Tangier, Agadir, Marrakech, and Fez. Infrastructure beyond football stadiums — high-speed rail links, airport expansions, hotel construction, and urban transport — received massive investment. The Casablanca Grand Stade project aimed to create one of the world's largest football stadiums. Morocco's World Cup preparations became a major driver of construction sector activity and employment.

title: Phosphate Diplomacy Deepens Africa Engagement
description: Morocco's OCP Group deepened its African fertiliser strategy in 2024, signing supply and investment agreements with multiple African governments to support local agricultural productivity. The African Fertilizer and Soil Health Summit reinforced OCP's positioning as a solution to African food insecurity. Morocco provided subsidised fertilisers to several low-income African countries. The phosphate diplomacy served both commercial interests and Morocco's broader strategy of building soft power and political influence across Africa.

title: Morocco Signs Green Hydrogen Agreement with Europe
description: Morocco concluded framework agreements with European partners including Germany and the European Commission in 2024 for the development and export of green hydrogen produced using solar and wind energy. The agreements envisaged Morocco as a major green energy supplier to Europe through undersea pipelines or liquefied hydrogen shipping. The green hydrogen ambition required enormous renewable energy investment but was seen as transformative for Morocco's long-term energy strategy and its economic relationship with Europe. Several pilot projects were funded in partnership with German and French development agencies.

title: Morocco Hosts Africa Cup of Nations Successfully
description: Morocco hosted the Africa Cup of Nations football tournament in January-February 2025, showcasing its upgraded stadium infrastructure and organisational capacity. The tournament was widely regarded as one of the best-organised AFCON editions, with high attendance, excellent playing surfaces, and smooth logistics. Morocco's national team performed well, reflecting the continued development of Moroccan football accelerated by the 2022 World Cup semi-final run. The successful hosting reinforced Morocco's claim to be ready for the larger challenge of co-hosting the 2030 World Cup.

title: Hirak Rif Political Prisoner Releases Debated
description: Human rights organisations intensified calls in 2025 for the release of Hirak Rif activists still imprisoned following the 2017 crackdown, including Nasser Zefzafi, who remained in prison. The continued imprisonment of social movement leaders despite years of international pressure highlighted the limits of Morocco's political reform. Domestic civil society organisations, Amazigh rights groups, and international human rights bodies maintained pressure on the government. The case of the Hirak prisoners remained one of the most prominent symbols of the gap between Morocco's reformist image and its treatment of political dissent.

title: Morocco's Economy Grows — Services and Manufacturing Diversify
description: By 2025 Morocco's economy had diversified significantly from its earlier reliance on phosphates, tourism, and agriculture, with automotive manufacturing, aerospace, electronics assembly, and offshoring services all making substantial contributions. The Tanger Med port complex had become the largest container port in Africa and the Mediterranean. GDP per capita had roughly doubled since 2000 in real terms. However, structural challenges persisted including high informal employment, regional inequality, youth unemployment, and dependence on rainfall for agricultural output.

title: Western Sahara Autonomy Plan Gains Additional International Recognition
description: Morocco's autonomy plan for Western Sahara, which proposed broad self-governance within Moroccan sovereignty, gained additional international endorsements in 2025, with several more European and African states declaring it a credible basis for a political solution. The UN Special Envoy Staffan de Mistura continued shuttle diplomacy between Morocco, the Polisario, Algeria, and Mauritania without achieving a breakthrough. The Polisario maintained its demand for a self-determination referendum while Morocco refused to accept any option other than autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty. The conflict thus entered its fifth decade without resolution.
